youtube.title: Skylab: How a Space Station Ended Up in a Teenager's Yard
youtube.description:
Skylab, America's first space station, came down on Western Australia in July 1979, and the little town of Esperance sent NASA a littering fine. How did a space station end up in a teenager's yard?

Just days ago NASA's Swift telescope ended its mission and is sinking toward Earth, pulled down by the same force that dropped Skylab: a stormy Sun. Skylab launched in 1973, was nearly lost on launch day, was rescued by its first crew with a giant sunshade and a cable cutter, and was left empty in 1974. Then the Sun puffed up our atmosphere, the Space Shuttle came too late, and the station fell.

In this video:
• How a Saturn V rocket stage became a space station
• The launch that tore off Skylab's shield and solar wing
• The umbrella and the spacewalk that saved it
• Why a stormy Sun pulled it down early
• Stan Thornton's race to San Francisco and NASA's A$400 littering fine

Subscribe to Stickstory for a true story like this every day. Should old spacecraft be brought down on purpose, or left to fall? Tell me in the comments!

#skylab #nasa #spacehistory #stickstory

scenes.text: Just after midnight, in July 1979, a quiet town in Western Australia woke up to a sound like thunder. But the sky was clear.
scenes.visual: Night over a small outback town (low houses with gold-lit windows, a water tank tower, a windmill) under a hatched night sky with stars; from the first frame a big glowing fireball with a gold-red trail streaks down from the top right and breaks into pieces, a second one follows; on 'thunder' ink sound rings and a red BOOM punch in the sky and the camera shakes; the fez narrator in the foreground looks up through binoculars, then jumps back in shock

scenes.text: Glowing pieces were streaking across the dark, breaking apart and falling.
scenes.visual: Closer on the night sky above the rooftops: three big fireballs race across the dark from the right, each splitting into a fan of smaller glowing pieces on 'breaking'; the fez narrator on the left points up at them, worried

scenes.text: A seventeen-year-old named Stan Thornton ran outside, and around his house he found burnt chunks of an American space station.
scenes.visual: Night yard of a house with a corrugated tin roof and a wire fence: smoking charred chunks drop onto the roof and the ground one after another; Stan, a bare-headed teenager, stands in the yard, then on 'chunks' bends and holds a smoking chunk; label 'Stan, 17'; the fez narrator on the right points at the chunks in shock

scenes.text: So how did a space station land in a teenager's yard? And why did his town send NASA a fine?
scenes.visual: Giant Fraunces words appear one by one: 'A space station' then 'in his yard?' with 'yard' in a red box; a handwritten red note 'and a fine?' pops up on 'fine'; a small fez narrator beside the words shrugs

scenes.text: Stick with me, because it's happening again. Just days ago, NASA's Swift telescope ended its science work, and it will soon fall into the atmosphere. And here's the twist: the same thing is pulling it down.
scenes.visual: Space above a big Earth limb with a blue air band: a small space telescope with two square solar panels rides a dashed orbit, label 'Swift, 2026'; on 'fall' it sinks toward the air band and on 'atmosphere' a red-gold flame trail grows behind it; the fez narrator in the corner points at it

scenes.text: The station was Skylab, America's first space station.
scenes.visual: CHAPTER 1 / 5 card: blue disc with 1, below it 'A Station Born Broken' with a hand-drawn underline

scenes.text: Engineers took the third stage of a giant Saturn Five Moon rocket and turned its empty fuel tank into a home,
scenes.visual: A hand-drawn Saturn V stands on its pad next to a lattice tower; label 'Saturn V' on 'Saturn'; on 'third' its third stage gets a red outline and pulses; on 'turned' that stage slides out of the stack, turns level, grows on the right and gets glowing windows, label 'home'; the fez narrator points at it

scenes.text: about seventy-seven tons, with more room than a small house.
scenes.visual: Skylab floats above the Earth limb, wrapped in its gold shield, both solar wings and the four windmill panels open; label '~77 tons' on 'tons'; on 'house' a small house outline pops up beside it for scale; the fez narrator points at the house

scenes.text: In May 1973, it launched. And about one minute into the flight, something went terribly wrong.
scenes.visual: The Saturn V lifts off: engines flare gold and red, white smoke billows out both sides, the rocket climbs past the tower; label 'May 14, 1973'; on 'wrong' a red burst flashes near the top and a gold shield flap tears off, the camera shakes; the fez narrator jumps back in shock

scenes.text: A thin metal shield, meant to block tiny space rocks and the heat of the Sun, tore loose.
scenes.visual: Close on Skylab in its gold shield with the Sun burning top right; on 'tore' a gold shield panel peels off the hull and spins away, the gold wrap is gone and the bare hull shows, the frame shakes; the fez narrator points then jumps in shock

scenes.text: Minutes later, one of the two big solar wings was ripped away, and a strip of metal pinned the other one shut.
scenes.visual: Skylab without its shield: on 'ripped' the top solar wing tears off and tumbles away out of frame, label 'gone'; the bottom wing lies folded flat against the hull with a red strap across it, on 'pinned' a red label 'stuck!' with an arrow; the fez narrator points at the strap

scenes.text: Now picture it. A brand new station with almost no power and no shade.
scenes.visual: Giant Fraunces words 'No power,' then 'no shade' with 'shade' in a red box; handwritten red note 'day one' with an arrow; the small fez narrator beside them holds his head, worried

scenes.text: Inside, it climbed to about fifty-four degrees Celsius.
scenes.visual: Bare Skylab with its missing wing under a blazing Sun, red heat squiggles rising off the hull; a big thermometer on the right climbs on 'climbed' and its reading turns to '54°C' in red; the fez narrator fans himself, worried

scenes.text: NASA had built a house in the sky, and it was baking. So who was going to fix it?
scenes.visual: The bare, damaged Skylab drifts under a blazing Sun with red heat squiggles; on 'house' a little house outline floats up beside it in the sky; on 'baking' red label 'baking'; on 'fix' the fez narrator turns to us and shrugs

scenes.text: Eleven days later, help was on the way.
scenes.visual: CHAPTER 2 / 5 card: blue disc with 2, below it 'The Rescue' with a hand-drawn underline

scenes.text: Three astronauts flew up: Pete Conrad, Joe Kerwin and Paul Weitz. Their first trick sounds almost silly.
scenes.visual: Three bare-headed astronauts walk in from the left one after another under a handwritten label 'Conrad, Kerwin, Weitz'; the fez narrator on the right points at them, then laughs on 'silly'

scenes.text: They pushed a folded sunshade, basically a giant umbrella, out through a tiny airlock, and opened it over the hot side. And it worked.
scenes.visual: Bare, overheated Skylab with a thermometer at '54°C' on the right: on 'pushed' a pole slides out of the top of the hull and a red fabric canopy unfolds over the hot side like an umbrella, label 'umbrella!'; on 'opened' the thermometer drops and turns blue, 'cooler'; on 'worked' green label 'it worked!'; the fez narrator cheers

scenes.text: But the station still needed power. So on the seventh of June, Conrad and Kerwin climbed outside with a long pole and a cable cutter.
scenes.visual: Close-up on the hull and the folded wing with its red strap; two helmeted spacewalkers with backpacks float beside the wing, slightly tilted and bobbing, the first reaches out a long pole with cutter jaws to the strap; label 'June 7, 1973'; the fez narrator points at the strap

scenes.text: Kerwin snipped the metal strap. The wing moved a little, then stuck again.
scenes.visual: Same close-up: on 'snipped' the cutter jaws snap shut, the red strap splits in two with a red ring flash; on 'moved' the wing lifts a little and stops, the frame jolts, red label 'stuck again'; the floating spacewalker shrugs; the fez narrator jumps

scenes.text: So they grabbed a rope, pulled with everything they had, and the wing swung open.
scenes.visual: Wider: the two spacewalkers pull a brown rope tied to the wing; on 'swung' the solar wing springs fully open below the hull with all its panels; green label 'power!'; the fez narrator throws his arms up

scenes.text: Skylab came back to life. Three crews lived there, and they studied the Sun like no one ever had.
scenes.visual: Horizontal timeline: 'May 1973' crew 1, 'Jul 1973' crew 2, 'Nov 1973' crew 3 (highlighted) appear one after another; a small fez narrator on the right points along it

scenes.text: Then, in February 1974, the last crew flew home.
scenes.visual: Skylab with the parasol and one wing: on 'flew' the docked Apollo ship backs off and flies away right with a gold engine flame; on 'home' the window lights go dark; label 'Feb 1974'; the fez narrator waves goodbye

scenes.text: Skylab was empty, and NASA thought it had years to decide what to do with it. But NASA was wrong.
scenes.visual: Giant Fraunces words 'NASA was wrong' appear word by word, 'wrong' in a red box on 'wrong'; handwritten note 'years?' on 'years'; the small fez narrator beside them jumps in shock

scenes.text: Here's the part most people never hear. Skylab didn't fall because it broke.
scenes.visual: CHAPTER 3 / 5 card: blue disc with 3, below it 'Why It Really Fell' with a hand-drawn underline

scenes.text: It fell because of the Sun.
scenes.visual: Open space: a big gold Sun with turning rays in the upper left, the Earth's curve at the bottom; on 'Sun' a red box stamp 'THE SUN' slams in; the fez narrator points at the Sun

scenes.text: Even four hundred kilometers up, there's a tiny trace of air, and it slowly steals the speed of anything flying through it.
scenes.visual: Earth limb with a thin blue air band dotted with tiny air dots; Skylab small on a dashed orbit high above; a red bracket '~400 km' from the ground to it on 'four'; on 'steals' a red speed arrow in front of Skylab shrinks while air dots hit its nose; the fez narrator points

scenes.text: When the Sun gets stormy, it heats that air, and the air puffs up like bread in an oven, reaching higher and grabbing harder.
scenes.visual: Same diagram with the Sun upper left: on 'stormy' red-gold bolts shoot from the Sun into the air band and the Sun pulses; on 'puffs' the blue air band swells up until it reaches Skylab's orbit, Skylab shakes and starts to sink; label 'puffs up!'; the fez narrator jumps back

scenes.text: NASA expected Skylab to last until around 1983. But the next solar cycle became one of the strongest in a century.
scenes.visual: Horizontal timeline: '1973' Skylab launch, '1983' NASA's guess, then '1979' the Sun's peak lights up red; a small fez narrator on the right points at 1979, worried

scenes.text: NASA had a rescue plan: the new Space Shuttle would fly up and push the station higher.
scenes.visual: Skylab drifts; on 'Shuttle' a hand-drawn Space Shuttle orbiter flies in from the lower right; on 'push' a red dashed arrow points up and the station lifts higher; label 'the plan'; the fez narrator points hopefully

scenes.text: But the Shuttle was late, and its first flight came only in 1981.
scenes.visual: Giant Fraunces words 'First Shuttle' then 'flight: 1981' with '1981' in a red box; handwritten note 'too late'; the small fez narrator shrugs

scenes.text: In December 1978, NASA gave up. A seventy-seven ton station was coming down.
scenes.visual: A bare-headed flight controller holds a sign 'GAVE UP' and lowers his head; on 'coming' the fez narrator next to him looks up and jumps back in shock; label 'Dec 1978'

scenes.text: So where would it land?
scenes.visual: A whole Earth globe in the middle; red dashed orbit tracks wrap around it one after another; a big red '?' pops up; the fez narrator looks through binoculars

scenes.text: Now imagine the summer of 1979. The whole world was looking up.
scenes.visual: CHAPTER 4 / 5 card: blue disc with 4, below it 'Where Will It Land?' with a hand-drawn underline

scenes.text: People sold T-shirts with a bullseye on them.
scenes.visual: Two T-shirts printed with red bullseyes swing on a clothesline; on 'bullseye' a dashed ink arrow drops from the sky onto the centre of the first one; the fez narrator laughs and points

scenes.text: One neighborhood in Nebraska painted a giant target, so the station would have something to aim for.
scenes.visual: A field with little houses on the horizon: on 'painted' a giant red-and-cream target spreads across the ground; two bare-headed painters hold rollers; on 'aim' a tiny ink Skylab with a red dashed trail drops toward the centre; label 'Nebraska'; the fez narrator shrugs

scenes.text: And the San Francisco Examiner made an offer: ten thousand dollars to the first person who brought a piece of Skylab to its office within seventy-two hours.
scenes.visual: A newspaper spins in and lands: masthead 'EXAMINER', huge red headline '$10,000', handwritten 'first piece wins'; on 'seventy' a stopwatch pops up on the right with a red hand ticking, label '72 h'; the fez narrator points at the headline

scenes.text: In the final hours, controllers set the station tumbling, to aim its fall at empty ocean southeast of South Africa.
scenes.visual: A big old map of the Indian Ocean: southern Africa on the left, Australia on the right, Cape Town and Perth marked; on 'aim' a red dashed path curves down from the west to an empty patch of ocean southeast of South Africa where a red ✗ in a ring appears, red note 'aim: empty ocean'; the fez narrator beside the map points at the ✗

scenes.text: On the eleventh of July, Skylab hit the thick air. And then came the surprise. It broke apart lower than predicted,
scenes.visual: Skylab tilted, plunging toward the Earth limb: on 'hit' red-gold flame tongues burst out and stream behind it, the hull glows with red hatching; label 'July 11, 1979'; on 'broke' its parts fly apart (wings, telescope mount, workshop, docking module), tumbling; the fez narrator jumps in shock, then points

scenes.text: and that small error carried its pieces over Western Australia, just after midnight.
scenes.visual: A big old map of south-west Australia: a red dashed debris path sweeps in from the ocean in the south-west across the coast near Esperance toward Balladonia, and a red hatched debris zone spreads around it; Esperance pops up in red, Perth and Balladonia marked; note 'just after midnight'; the fez narrator points at Esperance

scenes.text: But down in Esperance, a teenager was about to win a race.
scenes.visual: Stan, a bare-headed teenager, runs in from the left and stops holding up a sign 'SKYLAB!'; a clock prop on the right; the fez narrator runs after him and points at the clock on 'race'

scenes.text: Now, back to Stan.
scenes.visual: CHAPTER 5 / 5 card: blue disc with 5, below it 'A Fine for NASA' with a hand-drawn underline

scenes.text: Stan Thornton gathered about two dozen burnt pieces.
scenes.visual: Morning in Stan's yard by the tin-roofed house: charred, smoking chunks lie on the roof and all over the ground, more drop in; Stan holds one up; label '24 pieces'; the fez narrator points at the pile

scenes.text: He jumped on a plane and landed in San Francisco with hours to spare.
scenes.visual: A big old map of the Pacific: Australia lower left, the coast of North America upper right; a little ink plane flies along a red dashed route from Esperance to San Francisco; red note 'hours to spare'; the fez narrator points along the route

scenes.text: After NASA experts checked the pieces, Stan won the ten thousand dollars.
scenes.visual: Stan, a bare-headed teenager, holds up a giant cheque sign '$10,000' on 'won'; a scroll prop 'real!' beside him on 'checked'; the fez narrator claps and waves happily

scenes.text: Back home, Esperance had a sense of humor. When NASA officials came to see the wreckage, the shire handed them a fine of four hundred Australian dollars for littering.
scenes.visual: A ticket flies in: 'LITTERING' at the top, a big ink 'A$400', 'to: NASA'; a smoking charred chunk of Skylab lies beside it; on 'handed' a pen scribbles a signature; on 'littering' a red stamp 'FINED' slams onto the lower middle; the fez narrator laughs, then shocks

scenes.text: It was a joke, and NASA never paid. Not for thirty years.
scenes.visual: Horizontal timeline: '1979' the fine, '1989' unpaid, '1999' unpaid (highlighted) appear one after another; a small fez narrator on the right shrugs

scenes.text: Then, in 2009, an American radio host named Scott Barley asked his listeners to chip in, and they paid it.
scenes.visual: A radio microphone on the left sends out blue sound arcs; on 'chip' gold coins drop one by one into a glass jar; the A$400 ticket hangs on the right and on 'paid' a green stamp 'PAID' slams onto it; label '2009'; the fez narrator cheers

scenes.text: And here's what stays with me. Skylab wasn't killed by an accident in space. It was pulled down by a stormy Sun, just like Swift today.
scenes.visual: The Sun upper right above the Earth limb and air band; the damaged Skylab with its sunshade (label '1979') and the small Swift telescope (label 'today') ride the orbit; on 'stormy' bolts strike the air, it swells and both craft sink; the fez narrator points at the Sun

scenes.text: So, should old spacecraft be brought down on purpose, or left to fall where the sky decides?
scenes.visual: Two sign props: 'ON PURPOSE?' on the left and 'LET IT FALL?' on the right; the fez narrator in the middle points to the left sign on 'purpose', then to the right on 'fall', then shrugs at us on 'decides'

scenes.text: Tell me in the comments. And subscribe to Stickstory for a true story like this every day.
scenes.visual: Two sign props pop up: 'COMMENTS' on the left on 'comments', 'SUBSCRIBE' on the right on 'subscribe'; the fez narrator in the middle points at each, then waves at us on 'day'
